newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Better-than-expected trade data boost Slovak crown.
newsitem.headline: Better-than-expected trade data boost Slovak crown.

text.p: 1245 GMT - Slovak crown firms some 30 basis points in moderate Wednesday afternoon trade as dealers say better- than-expected trade data were one of several factors boosting crown buying sentiment.

*The crown strengthens to around -0.60 percent on the depreciation side of its the mark/dollar basket parity from about -0.95 percent on the basket's weak side shortly before the central bank (NBS) fixing at 0940 GMT.
*"Trade figures seemed to be better than the market expected and this helped boost appetite for crowns both from local and London banks," said Richard Brza of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.
*NBS Wednesday fixing, crown/dollar 34.884, crown/mark 18.979, deviation against the midpoint -1.01 percent.
The Slovak crown firmed some 30 basis points in moderate Wednesday afternoon trade as dealers said better-than-expected trade data was among several factors boosting crown buying sentiment.

At 1330 GMT the crown traded at around -0.50 percent on the depreciation side of its mark/dollar basket parity, stronger than about -0.95 percent on the basket's weak side shortly before the central bank (NBS) fixing at 0940 GMT.
"The trade figures seemed to be better than the market expected, and this helped boost appetite for crowns both from local and London banks," said Richard Brza of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.

"There could have also been some other factors behind the crown's firming, such as client orders or the typical Wednesday afternoon crown purchases to deposit crowns over the weekend," said Tibor Fratrik of ING Bank.
The crown usually strengthens by several basis points on Wednesday afternoons and subsequently weakens by around the same amount on Thursday mornings as buyers deposit crowns over the weekends.
Banks buy crowns on Wednesday and close the positions by buying back hard currencies on Thursday morning.
Wednesday deals are settled on Friday morning, while Thursday trades are settled on Monday, which give the crown deposits an extra day of interest rate yields.
Short-term funds on the local interbank traded at around 28 to 29 percent on Wednesday.
"The usual Thursday crown selling could weaken it to around -0.80 percent (on the basket's weak side).
"But it is quite difficult to predict any longer-term trend as the market remains very narrow which means low volumes can spark a rather significant move," Brza said.
Traders predicted the crown could move between the basket's central parity and some -1.50 percent on the weak side later this week.
The NBS on Wednesday fixed the crown at 34.884 to the dollar and at 18.979 to the mark, implying a deviation of -1.01 percent against the midpoint .
